covers: The clock, status and RAM bytes of the MC146818

entries.name: seconds
entries.behaviour: Holds the seconds, 0 to 59, in BCD or binary as bit 2 of status register B selects. Bit 7 is read only. The chip advances it as time passes.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses a value over 59, and in BCD mode invalid BCD; MAME stores the byte with bit 7 cleared.

entries.name: seconds alarm
entries.behaviour: Holds the alarm seconds in BCD or binary as bit 2 of status register B selects. A value with bits 7 and 6 both set matches any second.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses a value over 59, and in BCD mode invalid BCD, so it never holds one with bits 7 and 6 set; MAME stores the byte as written and lets it match any second.

entries.name: minutes
entries.behaviour: Holds the minutes, 0 to 59, in BCD or binary as bit 2 of status register B selects. The chip advances it as time passes.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses a value over 59, and in BCD mode invalid BCD; MAME stores the byte as written.

entries.name: minutes alarm
entries.behaviour: Holds the alarm minutes in BCD or binary as bit 2 of status register B selects. A value with bits 7 and 6 both set matches any minute.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses a value over 59, and in BCD mode invalid BCD, so it never holds one with bits 7 and 6 set; MAME stores the byte as written and lets it match any minute.

entries.name: hours
entries.behaviour: Holds the hours in BCD or binary as bit 2 of status register B selects: 0 to 23 in 24-hour mode, 1 to 12 in 12-hour mode with bit 7 set for PM. Bit 1 of status register B selects the mode.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses an hour out of range for the mode, and in BCD mode invalid BCD; its BCD PM hours 0x81 to 0x89 convert wrongly (0x81 stores 23, 0x83 is refused). MAME stores the byte as written.

entries.name: hours alarm
entries.behaviour: Holds the alarm hours in the same form as the hours. A value with bits 7 and 6 both set matches any hour; the alarm flag is set when seconds, minutes and hours all match.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses an out-of-range hour, invalid BCD in BCD mode, and bits 7 and 6 set; it converts BCD PM hours 0x81 to 0x89 wrongly. MAME stores the byte as written and lets bits 7 and 6 match any hour.

entries.name: day of week
entries.description: Day of the week of the clock.
entries.behaviour: Holds the day of the week, 1 to 7 with Sunday as 1, in BCD or binary as bit 2 of status register B selects. The chip advances it at midnight.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses a value outside 1 to 7, and in BCD mode invalid BCD; MAME stores the byte as written.

entries.name: day of month
entries.description: Day of the month of the clock.
entries.behaviour: Holds the day of the month, 1 to 31, in BCD or binary as bit 2 of status register B selects. The chip advances it at midnight and wraps it at the end of the month.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses a value outside 1 to 31, and in BCD mode invalid BCD; MAME stores the byte as written.

entries.name: month
entries.behaviour: Holds the month, 1 to 12, in BCD or binary as bit 2 of status register B selects. The chip advances it at the end of the month.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses a value outside 1 to 12, and in BCD mode invalid BCD; MAME stores the byte as written.

entries.name: year
entries.description: Year of the clock within its century.
entries.behaviour: Holds the year, 0 to 99, in BCD or binary as bit 2 of status register B selects. The chip advances it at the end of December.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X refuses a value over 99, and in BCD mode invalid BCD; MAME stores the byte as written.

entries.name: status A
entries.description: Status register A: the time base, the periodic interrupt rate and the update-in-progress flag.
entries.behaviour: Bits 3 to 0 select the periodic interrupt rate and bits 6 to 4 the time base divider. Bit 7 is read only and is set while the clock updates.

entries.name: status B
entries.description: Status register B: the interrupt enables, the update freeze and the data format.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 freezes updates so the clock can be set, and setting it clears bit 4. Bits 6, 5 and 4 enable the periodic, alarm and update-ended interrupts, bit 3 the square wave, bit 2 selects binary over BCD, bit 1 the 24-hour mode and bit 0 daylight saving, which MAME does not apply.

entries.name: status C
entries.description: Status register C, read only: which interrupt conditions occurred.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 is the interrupt request flag, bit 6 the periodic, bit 5 the alarm and bit 4 the update-ended flag; bits 3 to 0 read 0. A read clears every flag.

sources.cites: CMOS 0Ch - RTC - STATUS REGISTER C (Read only)

against.line: CMOS 0Ch - RTC - STATUS REGISTER C (Read only)

entries.name: status D
entries.description: Status register D, read only: whether the clock's battery kept its RAM valid.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 set means the battery kept the RAM and the time valid; bits 6 to 0 read 0. The chip's register is read only.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X holds bit 7 from the start, returns it unchanged on a read and keeps bit 7 of a write; MAME sets it only after a read (unless its RAM was loaded) and ignores a write.

sources.cites: CMOS 0Dh - RTC - STATUS REGISTER D (read only)

entries.name: general purpose RAM
entries.description: The battery-backed RAM bytes after the clock registers.
entries.behaviour: A write stores the byte and a read returns it. The first fourteen bytes are the clock and its status registers, so these are the bytes left over.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X computes the floppy and disk bytes (0x10, 0x12, 0x19 to 0x2C) from its drives, reads 0x39 and 0x3A as 0, keeps 7 bits at 0x0F, and keeps the clock's century at 0x32 and 0x37; MAME holds plain RAM.

sources.cites: The first fourteen bytes are dedicated to the MC146818 chip clock functions
